PullRequest.Title: Agents window: adopt author-first editor comment cards
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- Replace editor comment bubbles with author-first cards, quiet line metadata, inline actions and independent three-line previews with See more/See less.
- Keep More Actions visible, separate header buttons on the spacing ramp, and use the existing frosted-glass treatment and accessibility fallbacks.
- Preserve editing, replies, PR reviewer attribution and navigation. This is limited to code-editor comment widgets; optimized Markdown editor cards are unchanged.

## Issues addressed

| Severity | Issue | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| P2 | A rebuilt submitted/resolved card could reopen an editable draft. | Suspend composer restoration in readonly states while retaining the draft; cover real contribution-driven state transitions. |
| P2 | Blanket chat Markdown options blocked images in ordinary human comments and replies. | Apply chat restrictions to known agent-authored content and retain the existing human-comment image policy. |
| P2 | Widening a responsive card left its horizontal-scroll reservation stale. | Invalidate the cached reservation before publishing layout when rendered width changes; verify that covered code can be revealed in a real editor. |
| P2 | Always-visible card stacks could extend beyond the editor, and bounded stacks need to reveal navigation targets. | Add a named keyboard-focusable scroll region only when needed, contain wheel scrolling, reveal offscreen cards, and preserve the reading position of an already-visible long card. |

The fixture command uses a temporary, uncommitted Vite adapter for JSONC theme imports and the browser path alias. Four representative fixtures were hash-identical immediately after rendering, after idle, and after remount. A temporary native-input probe verified ArrowDown scrolling, wheel scrolling without moving the underlying editor, and reaching the final card.

The new layout regressions were demonstrated failing before the fixes and passing afterward. The detached-baseline dependency bootstrap encountered npm E401 during supplemental postinstall; required fixture dependencies were available and baseline rendering passed. No credentials or registry configuration were changed.

### How to test

1. In an Agents session, open a changed code file with human, agent and PR review comments.
2. Check short and long previews, See more/See less, always-visible More Actions, Edit, Add to Comment, sharing and readonly review states.
3. Resize the editor; verify code can scroll out from under the cards and large card stacks remain reachable by keyboard, wheel and comment navigation.
4. Toggle the existing frosted-glass setting and opacity, then check light, dark and high-contrast themes.

## Visual evidence

Before images use detached `main` at `aaf0914f8ba`; after images use the reviewed branch. Both pairs use the same synthetic fixture data, Dark theme and 760x420 editor, with identical 762x422 crops. ## Review status

- Unresolved actionable code findings: None
- Required CI: Pending
- Residual risks: Full smoke/integration suites and live provider flows were not run.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The hot call path and multiplicity are explicit in repository code, and the diff directly adds the per-comment DOM measurements to it. Exact milliseconds depend on card count and markdown size, which affects severity but not mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous DOM style/layout calculations for every comment preview
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with editor scroll event frequency multiplied by the number of comment widgets and comments in each grouped widget; expanded previews additionally perform a class write, geometry reads, and a restoring write on every event.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased main-thread layout work and dropped frames while scrolling comment-heavy files
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The contribution already repositioned each widget on editor scroll, but the old layout path performed only a constant number of widget-level geometry reads and did not remeasure every comment preview.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The changed layout method now calls _updateTextPreviews on every relayout; that helper iterates all previews, toggles the collapsed class, and reads clientHeight/scrollHeight before layout continues with more body/widget measurements.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1010 adds `this._updateTextPreviews();` to `layout()`, which is transitively called for every editor scroll by the contribution; the helper and its per-comment geometry reads are also introduced by this diff.
Findings.Title: Keep preview measurement off the editor scroll path
Findings.Impact: With realistic grouped stacks such as the ten-card case covered by the added tests, every trackpad/wheel scroll synchronously remeasures all preview DOM even though scrolling does not change truncation. Long or expanded markdown cards can therefore make editor scrolling visibly janky.
Findings.Evidence: AgentFeedbackEditorWidgetContribution.ts:67-70 invokes widget.relayout() for every onDidScrollChange. The added call at AgentFeedbackEditorWidget.ts:1010 enters _updateTextPreviews; lines 454-462 show its per-preview clientHeight/scrollHeight reads and collapsed-class mutations, and layout then reads body.scrollHeight/offsetHeight/clientHeight. This changes the existing scroll path from O(widgets) widget positioning to O(comments) preview measurement plus widget geometry.
Findings.Recommendation: Separate position-only scroll relayout from size/content relayout. Recompute preview truncation only when card content or available width changes (for example from the resize observer), cache the result, and batch DOM writes before geometry reads.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The one-filter-per-card DOM/CSS relationship and scrolling scenario are explicit. Hardware-specific GPU cost is uncertain, so severity is medium, but independent backdrop filtering over changing editor content is a concrete rendering mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Independent compositor/backdrop-filter surfaces and blurred pixels for each visible comment card
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Rendering cost grows with the number and painted area of visible cards on every frame whose editor backdrop or card position changes; the PR's own oversized-stack scenario renders ten cards.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher GPU/compositor load and dropped frames while scrolling or resizing editors with comment stacks
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Agent feedback cards were not selected by the frosted-glass surface rule, so they used an opaque background and created no 12px backdrop-filter layers.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added selector makes every `.agent-feedback-widget-item` instantiate the shared `::before` surface, whose rule applies `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)`. A grouped stack therefore creates one persistent blur surface per card.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 90 newly includes `.agent-feedback-widget-item` in the selector whose `::before` applies the 12px backdrop filter; before this PR comment cards were absent from that selector.
Findings.Title: Avoid a backdrop-filter surface for every comment card
Findings.Impact: When frosted glass is enabled, scrolling code underneath an always-visible multi-card stack requires recompositing multiple full-card blur regions each frame, making editor scrolling and resize less smooth as the stack grows.
Findings.Evidence: The added `.agent-feedback-widget-item` selector at line 90 joins the common surface rule; lines 95-106 define an absolute full-card pseudo-element with `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)`. The changed widget renders one `.agent-feedback-widget-item` per comment, and the added OversizedCommentStack fixture explicitly models ten visible cards.
Findings.Recommendation: Consolidate frosted rendering to at most one backdrop-filter surface per widget/stack (using masking/clipping if gaps must remain clear), or keep repeated cards translucent without applying backdrop-filter individually.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an editor containing agent feedback and PR review comments
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor contribution synchronously gathers session comments, filters and groups them, constructs one overlay widget per group, renders every comment/reply Markdown node, and lays out the overlays before the cards are usable.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: All comments for the active session are scanned, then the comments for the current resource are rendered; effective DOM cardinality is one card per file comment grouped into one or more widgets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All grouping, Markdown rendering, DOM construction, and initial layout run synchronously on the UI thread; there is no limiter or deferred card virtualization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The feedback backend supplies a local session cache, and minimum content width is cached after real width/line measurements. Card preview measurements are not cached. Cold and warm rendering still rebuild all widget DOM when the contribution's rebuild signals fire.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: construction and grouping paths were inspected directly. The diff adds more card chrome but eager Markdown rendering already existed, so no independent eager-work finding was submitted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Files with many simultaneous comments are less common than small reviews, but the added tests establish realistic ten-card stacks. Markdown complexity varies by provider content.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression beyond the reported layout/rendering findings: eager Markdown work remains broadly consistent with the pre-diff widget, while author metadata and toolbars add bounded per-card work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll or resize an editor with visible comment cards, including frosted-glass mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every editor scroll/layout event synchronously calls relayout on every widget before the frame can settle. Relayout now remeasures each preview and widget geometry; with frosted glass, compositor output also includes one 12px backdrop blur per card.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with scroll/resize event frequency, widget count, comments per grouped widget, expanded Markdown size, and—for frosted glass—the visible pixel area of every card. A ten-card stack is explicitly covered by the PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM measurement and style mutation is serialized on the UI thread. Browser compositor work occurs per frame; there is no coalescing or shared blur surface for the repeated cards.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Minimum horizontal width has a widget-width cache, but preview truncation is remeasured on every relayout even when scrolling cannot change it. Frosted surfaces are persistent and have no cardinality bound beyond visible cards.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the scroll listener, relayout call chain, geometry reads/class writes, CSS selector, and backdrop-filter declaration were all traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact layout and GPU duration depends on card count, Markdown height, browser, GPU, and whether frosted glass is enabled; the hot path and one-filter-per-card scaling are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Two reportable regressions were submitted: synchronous per-comment preview measurement on the editor scroll path and independent backdrop-filter surfaces for every card.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load PR review state and backfill authors on persisted mirror annotations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Once PR review state and the authoritative feedback snapshot are loaded, the seeder synchronously scans feedback/comments and dispatches an annotation upsert for each legacy mirror that has pull-request identity but lacks an author. Dispatch is not awaited, so remote acknowledgement is off the immediate card-display critical path, though optimistic cache updates and feedback events occur synchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch an annotations/set action carrying the updated feedback annotation to the agent-host connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch for each loaded legacy PR mirror lacking author; zero after successful persistence/echo, plus pre-existing dispatches for newly seeded or changed comments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Mirrors that already had sourcePullRequest data were skipped, so author-only backfill produced no dispatch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Optimistic local cache mutation and event emission are synchronous; host acknowledgement is not awaited and is off the immediate display critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective new boundary cardinality is one annotations-set dispatch per legacy mirrored PR comment missing author. New mirrors include authors immediately, and persisted/echoed backfills make subsequent warm runs zero for those items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The seeder loops sequentially but dispatches without a shared asynchronous limiter; a cold legacy session can issue a burst proportional to missing-author mirrors.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The persisted author field acts as the positive migration marker. Cold legacy entries miss it and are updated once; warm entries skip. Empty upstream authors are not written, so they remain eligible but do not dispatch until a non-empty author exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the per-missing-author dispatch and warm-cache behavior; lower magnitude risk because the migration is bounded by legacy review comments and becomes self-disabling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Legacy sessions may contain few or many mirrored comments, and connection dispatch cost is not measured. The work is a one-time metadata migration rather than recurring warm-path fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: although the diff introduces cold per-comment IPC backfill, it is a bounded one-time migration with an explicit persisted marker and is not on a waited critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit, reply to, accept, hide, or resolve a comment card
Scenarios.CriticalPath: User activation updates the composer/card synchronously, then invokes the existing feedback or code-review mutation. Relayout runs after local DOM changes so the card can resize.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upsert accepted/edited/replied feedback through the annotations connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one relevant feedback mutation per user action; unchanged in cardinality by this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same feedback actions already crossed the annotations boundary; the PR changes presentation and preserves author metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The optimistic update is immediate and remote acknowledgement is not synchronously awaited by these card handlers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a pull-request review thread through the code-review service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per explicit resolve action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The widget already invoked resolvePRReviewThread once; the diff supplies pull-request identity and returns the existing promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The returned promise represents remote resolution, but the user explicitly initiated the action; no loop or added fan-out is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One mutation and one local relayout per explicit user action; reply Markdown rendering scales with that comment's replies, not the whole session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Actions execute individually through the toolbar action runner. There is no collection-wide concurrent burst introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Composer drafts are retained across contribution rebuilds and pruned when comments disappear. The feedback backend updates its optimistic cache before dispatching the remote mutation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: action handlers and backend boundaries were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote provider latency varies, but call count and placement are unchanged. Local relayout cost for composer typing is covered by content changes rather than the scroll-path finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional regression: boundary cardinality remains one per user action, draft retention is bounded and pruned, and the changed metadata does not add remote calls.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 21 changed files. Reported two medium-confidence-impact regressions with high mechanism confidence: per-comment synchronous preview measurement on every editor scroll, and one backdrop-filter compositor surface per frosted comment card. Checked eager rendering, caches, lifecycle cleanup, PR-author migration IPC fan-out, and user-action boundaries; no other diff-caused issue met the reporting threshold.
